candidates.text: The President is the only person who alone composes a branch of government. As a result, there is not always a clear line between his personal and official affairs.
candidates.speaker: Roberts
phrases: only person who alone composes a branch of government
candidates.reason: States why separation-of-powers scrutiny reaches a President's personal records, the premise of the case's rule; also the most quoted line.

candidates.text: The President's unique constitutional position means that Congress may not look to him as a `case study' for general legislation.
candidates.speaker: Roberts
phrases: may not look to him as a case study for general legislation

candidates.text: I would hold that Congress has no power to issue a legislative subpoena for private, nonofficial documents
candidates.speaker: Thomas, dissenting
candidates.reason: Main dissent, the impeachment-channeling problem in the Critique.

candidates.text: Congress and the President---the two political branches established by the Constitution---have an ongoing relationship
candidates.speaker: Roberts
phrases: ongoing relationship that the Framers intended to feature both rivalry and reciprocity
